# Certified Fractional Chromatic Bounds from Implicit Column Generation — Reproducibility Artifact

**Article:** Certified Fractional Chromatic Bounds from Implicit Column Generation  
**Author:** Husain M. Naser  

This compact artifact supports the machine-checkable and aggregate computational claims reported in the article. It contains per-instance outcome tables, input identity manifests, exact-clique strength audits, the retrospective certified-endpoint portfolio, the Erdős–Rényi certificate-size analysis, the fixed separator-reuse experiment, selected reference source modules, and verification scripts.

Third-party executables and benchmark archives are not redistributed in this compact package. Exact third-party identities used in the evaluation are recorded in `provenance/SOFTWARE_IDENTITIES.md`.

**Archival record:** https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21981971  
**Source-browsing mirror:** https://github.com/HusainNaser/certified-fractional-chromatic-bounds

## Main verified counts

- Primary evaluation: 67/116 DIMACS and 974/1000 Erdős–Rényi endpoints pass mapping, VeriPB, and CakePB: **1,041 formal certificates** in total.
- Exact-clique strength of the primary evaluation: **at least 812** certificates yield integer lower bounds strictly larger than exact clique.
- Additional-column proposal method: 73/116 DIMACS and 737/1000 Erdős–Rényi formal certificates; it is reported as a proposal-quality mechanism study, not as the primary evaluation.
- Retrospective certified portfolio over the two proposal methods: **1,066** distinct formal certificates, **at least 840** strict improvements over exact clique, 225 clique-equivalent, and one exact-clique-unclassified DIMACS case.
- DIMACS additional-column-only strength audit: 13 cases, with 11 clique numbers recomputed locally and two values (`DSJC500.9=54`, `latin_square_10=90`) attributed to Held, Cook and Sewell (2012) after fixed-resource local exact attempts did not complete.

## Quick verification

From the extracted artifact root, run:

```bash
python3 verification/verify_artifact.py
```

A successful run prints `ARTIFACT_VERIFY_PASS`.

## Evidence boundary

This is a compact reviewer/public artifact. It does not duplicate the largest PBP/kernel objects or raw console logs. Four public full-evidence archives containing generated exact-pricing records, proof objects, kernels, mapping evidence, and checker logs are companion files on the same Zenodo record. Their filenames, SHA-256 identities, sizes, and provenance are recorded in `provenance/FULL_EVIDENCE_PUBLIC_RELEASE.md`. The tables here are sufficient to regenerate and check the aggregate counts reported in the manuscript without downloading those large archives.
